title: QUIC RFC 9250 Requirements
scope: This specification covers DNS over QUIC adapter requirements, including ALPN, default port behavior, DNS message framing, query and response stream lifecycle, protocol errors, connection lifecycle, 0-RTT and replay policy, flow-control mapping, response ordering, and registry governance.
context: DNS over QUIC behavior is layered above the shared QUIC transport runtime. The DoQ adapter owns DNS message and stream semantics while shared QUIC transport requirements continue to own packet protection, stream limits, flow control, TLS, and transport-parameter mechanics.

requirements.title: Avoid path MTU limits on DNS response size
requirements.statement: The DoQ transport MUST NOT impose path MTU limitations on the size of DNS responses it can send.

requirements.title: Map each DNS query/response transaction to a separate stream
requirements.statement: Each DNS Query/Response transaction MUST be mapped to a separate stream to mitigate head-of-line blocking.

requirements.title: Negotiate TLS security parameters during QUIC setup
requirements.statement: QUIC connection setup MUST negotiate security parameters using TLS.
notes: Trimmed to the smallest independently testable obligation; the RFC9001 reference is preserved in upstream trace rather than the requirement text.

requirements.title: Indicate DoQ support with ALPN token doq
requirements.statement: During connection establishment, DoQ support MUST be indicated by selecting the Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation (ALPN) token "doq" in the crypto handshake.
notes: Single testable invariant; wording already minimal and traceable.

requirements.title: Listen on UDP port 853 by default
requirements.statement: A DNS server that supports DoQ MUST listen for and accept QUIC connections on the dedicated UDP port 853, unless there is a mutual agreement to use another port.

requirements.title: Connect to UDP port 853 by default
requirements.statement: A DNS client desiring to use DoQ with a particular server MUST establish a QUIC connection to UDP port 853 on the server, unless there is a mutual agreement to use another port.

requirements.title: Disallow UDP port 53
requirements.statement: A DoQ connection MUST NOT use UDP port 53.

requirements.title: Select a separate QUIC stream for each query
requirements.statement: The client MUST select a separate QUIC stream for each query.

requirements.title: Use one stream for all responses to a query
requirements.statement: The server MUST use the same stream to provide all response messages for that query.

requirements.title: Encode DNS messages with a 2-octet length field
requirements.statement: All DNS messages sent over DoQ connections MUST be encoded as a 2-octet length field followed by the message content as specified in [RFC1035].

requirements.title: Select the next available client-initiated bidirectional stream
requirements.statement: The client MUST select the next available client-initiated bidirectional stream for each subsequent query on a QUIC connection.

requirements.title: Process queries as they arrive
requirements.statement: Servers SHOULD process queries as they arrive.

requirements.title: Send DNS query on selected stream
requirements.statement: A client MUST send the DNS query over the selected stream.

requirements.title: Signal end of client stream with STREAM FIN
requirements.statement: A client MUST indicate through the STREAM FIN mechanism that no further data will be sent on that stream.

requirements.title: Send responses on the same stream
requirements.statement: The server MUST send the response(s) on the same stream.

requirements.title: Signal end of server stream with STREAM FIN
requirements.statement: The server MUST indicate, after the last response, through the STREAM FIN mechanism that no further data will be sent on that stream.

requirements.title: Map client queries to QUIC client-initiated streams in order
requirements.statement: The client's first query MUST occur on QUIC stream 0, the second on 4, and so on.

requirements.title: Allow deferred processing until client STREAM FIN
requirements.statement: A server MAY defer processing of a query until the STREAM FIN has been indicated on the stream selected by the client.

requirements.title: Monitor dangling streams
requirements.statement: Servers and clients MAY monitor the number of dangling streams.

requirements.title: Impose a limit on dangling streams
requirements.statement: Implementations MAY impose a limit on the number of such dangling streams.

requirements.title: Close the connection when limits are encountered
requirements.statement: If limits are encountered, implementations MAY close the connection.

requirements.title: Set DNS Message ID to zero
requirements.statement: When sending queries over a QUIC connection, the DNS Message ID MUST be set to 0.

requirements.title: DoQ stream mapping does not require Message ID
requirements.statement: The DoQ stream mapping MUST allow unambiguous correlation of queries and responses without requiring the Message ID field.

requirements.title: Generate Message ID when forwarding from DoQ
requirements.statement: When forwarding a DNS message from DoQ over another transport, a DNS Message ID MUST be generated according to the rules of the protocol that is in use.

requirements.title: Set Message ID to zero when forwarding to DoQ
requirements.statement: When forwarding a DNS message from another transport over DoQ, the Message ID MUST be set to 0.

requirements.title: DOQ_NO_ERROR indicates no error
requirements.statement: DOQ_NO_ERROR (0x0) MUST indicate that there is no error.
notes: Wording trimmed to the smallest standalone invariant.

requirements.title: Use DOQ_NO_ERROR when closing without error
requirements.statement: The DOQ_NO_ERROR code MUST be used when the connection or stream needs to be closed, but there is no error to signal.
notes: Keeps the usage condition and removes extra framing.

requirements.title: Use DOQ_INTERNAL_ERROR for unrecoverable internal failures
requirements.statement: A DoQ implementation MUST use DOQ_INTERNAL_ERROR (0x1) when it encounters an internal error and is incapable of pursuing the transaction or the connection.
notes: Captures the trigger condition as a single testable invariant.

requirements.title: Use DOQ_PROTOCOL_ERROR for protocol failures
requirements.statement: A DoQ implementation MUST use DOQ_PROTOCOL_ERROR (0x2) when it encounters a protocol error and is forcibly aborting the connection.
notes: Keeps only the protocol-error trigger and required code.

requirements.title: Use DOQ_REQUEST_CANCELLED to cancel an outstanding transaction
requirements.statement: A DoQ client MUST use DOQ_REQUEST_CANCELLED (0x3) to signal that it wants to cancel an outstanding transaction.
notes: Preserves the client-only trigger and cancellation intent.

requirements.title: Use DOQ_EXCESSIVE_LOAD when closing due to excessive load
requirements.statement: A DoQ implementation MUST use DOQ_EXCESSIVE_LOAD (0x4) to signal when closing a connection due to excessive load.
notes: Trims the sentence to the required close-on-load condition.

requirements.title: Use DOQ_UNSPECIFIED_ERROR when no specific code applies
requirements.statement: A DoQ implementation MUST use DOQ_UNSPECIFIED_ERROR (0x5) in the absence of a more specific error code.
notes: Keeps the fallback-code condition explicit and testable.

requirements.title: Reserved test error code may be used for tests
requirements.statement: DOQ_ERROR_RESERVED (0xd098ea5e) MAY be used for tests.
notes: Retains the reserved test-code allowance with minimal wording.

requirements.title: STOP_SENDING requests peer cease transmission
requirements.statement: Sending STOP_SENDING MUST request that a peer cease transmission on a stream.

requirements.title: Cancel outstanding request with STOP_SENDING
requirements.statement: A DoQ client that wishes to cancel an outstanding request MUST issue a QUIC STOP_SENDING.

requirements.title: Prefer DOQ_REQUEST_CANCELLED for cancellation
requirements.statement: A DoQ client that cancels an outstanding request SHOULD use the error code DOQ_REQUEST_CANCELLED.

requirements.title: Discard response after late STOP_SENDING
requirements.statement: If the server response has already been sent, the client MUST discard the incoming response.

requirements.title: Send STOP_SENDING at any time
requirements.statement: A DoQ client MAY send a STOP_SENDING request at any time.

requirements.title: Use registered specific error code
requirements.statement: A DoQ client MAY use a more specific error code registered according to Section 8.4.

requirements.title: Abandon corresponding DNS transaction
requirements.statement: The corresponding DNS transaction MUST be abandoned.

requirements.title: Stop processing after STOP_SENDING
requirements.statement: Servers SHOULD NOT continue processing a DNS transaction if they receive a STOP_SENDING.

requirements.title: Limit cancellation request volume
requirements.statement: Servers MAY impose implementation limits on the total number or rate of cancellation requests.

requirements.title: Close connection on cancellation limits
requirements.statement: If limits are encountered, servers MAY close the connection.

requirements.title: Use DOQ_EXCESSIVE_LOAD for debugging
requirements.statement: Servers wanting to help client debugging MAY use the error code DOQ_EXCESSIVE_LOAD.

requirements.title: Stop processing on early RESET_STREAM
requirements.statement: Servers MUST NOT continue processing a DNS transaction if they receive a RESET_STREAM request from the client before the client indicates the STREAM FIN.

requirements.title: Issue RESET_STREAM unless already reset or response complete
requirements.statement: The server MUST issue a RESET_STREAM to indicate that the transaction is abandoned unless it has already done so for another reason or it has already sent the response and indicated the STREAM FIN.

requirements.title: Notify client of SERVFAIL with SERVFAIL response
requirements.statement: A client SHOULD be notified of SERVFAIL through a response whose Response Code is set to SERVFAIL.

requirements.title: Issue RESET_STREAM on internal error
requirements.statement: If a server cannot send a DNS response because of an internal error, it SHOULD issue a QUIC RESET_STREAM frame.

requirements.title: Set RESET_STREAM error code to DOQ_INTERNAL_ERROR
requirements.statement: The error code SHOULD be set to DOQ_INTERNAL_ERROR.

requirements.title: Abandon the corresponding DNS transaction
requirements.statement: The corresponding DNS transaction MUST be abandoned.

requirements.title: Limit unsolicited RESET_STREAM frames before closing
requirements.statement: Clients MAY limit unsolicited QUIC RESET_STREAM frames received on a connection before closing it.

requirements.title: Protocol error: non-zero Message ID
requirements.statement: If a client or server receives a message with a non-zero Message ID, it MUST treat this as a fatal error.

requirements.title: Protocol error: STREAM FIN before complete message
requirements.statement: If a client or server receives a STREAM FIN before receiving all the bytes for a message indicated in the 2-octet length field, it MUST treat this as a fatal error.

requirements.title: Protocol error: early STREAM FIN
requirements.statement: If a client receives a STREAM FIN before receiving all the expected responses, it MUST treat this as a fatal error.

requirements.title: Protocol error: multiple queries on a stream
requirements.statement: If a server receives more than one query on a stream, it MUST treat this as a fatal error.

requirements.title: Protocol error: unexpected response count
requirements.statement: If a client receives a different number of responses on a stream than expected, it MUST treat this as a fatal error.

requirements.title: Protocol error: receiving STOP_SENDING
requirements.statement: If a client receives a STOP_SENDING request, it MUST treat this as a fatal error.

requirements.title: Protocol error: missing expected STREAM FIN
requirements.statement: If the client or server does not indicate the expected STREAM FIN after sending requests or responses, it MUST treat this as a fatal error.

requirements.title: Protocol error: edns-tcp-keepalive option
requirements.statement: If an implementation receives a message containing the edns-tcp-keepalive EDNS(0) Option, it MUST treat this as a fatal error.

requirements.title: Protocol error: opening a unidirectional stream
requirements.statement: If a client or a server attempts to open a unidirectional QUIC stream, it MUST treat this as a fatal error.

requirements.title: Protocol error: opening a server-initiated bidirectional stream
requirements.statement: If a server attempts to open a server-initiated bidirectional QUIC stream, it MUST treat this as a fatal error.

requirements.title: Abort the connection with CONNECTION_CLOSE
requirements.statement: A DoQ endpoint SHOULD forcibly abort the connection using QUIC's CONNECTION_CLOSE mechanism.

requirements.title: Use DOQ_PROTOCOL_ERROR
requirements.statement: A DoQ endpoint SHOULD use the DoQ error code DOQ_PROTOCOL_ERROR.

requirements.title: Treat unknown or unexpected error codes as unspecified
requirements.statement: An implementation MUST treat use of an error code in an unexpected context or receipt of an unknown error code as equivalent to DOQ_UNSPECIFIED_ERROR.

requirements.title: Negotiate idle timeout
requirements.statement: DoQ endpoints SHOULD negotiate the idle timeout.

requirements.title: Idle timeout effective value
requirements.statement: The effective idle timeout MUST be the minimum of the two endpoints' advertised values.

requirements.title: Monitor server idle time
requirements.statement: Clients SHOULD monitor server idle time, defined as the time since the last packet from the server was received.

requirements.title: Check idle time before sending a query
requirements.statement: When a client prepares to send a new DNS query to the server, it SHOULD check whether the idle time is sufficiently lower than the idle timer.

requirements.title: Send query over existing connection when idle time permits
requirements.statement: If the client's idle time is sufficiently lower than the idle timer, the client SHOULD send the DNS query over the existing connection.

requirements.title: Open a new connection when idle time is not low enough
requirements.statement: If the client's idle time is not sufficiently lower than the idle timer, the client SHOULD establish a new connection and send the query over that connection.

requirements.title: Discard connections before idle timeout
requirements.statement: Clients MAY discard server connections before the idle timeout expires.

requirements.title: Close outstanding queries explicitly
requirements.statement: A client with outstanding queries SHOULD close the connection explicitly using QUIC's CONNECTION_CLOSE mechanism.

requirements.title: Use DOQ_NO_ERROR on explicit close
requirements.statement: A client with outstanding queries SHOULD use the DoQ error code DOQ_NO_ERROR when closing the connection explicitly.

requirements.title: Allow other reasons for connection close
requirements.statement: Clients and servers MAY close the connection using QUIC's CONNECTION_CLOSE for other reasons.

requirements.title: Abandon in-progress transactions on connection failure
requirements.statement: If a connection fails, all the in-progress transactions on that connection MUST be abandoned.

requirements.title: Allow session resumption and 0-RTT when supported
requirements.statement: A client MAY use session resumption and 0-RTT if the server supports them.
notes: Trimmed the transport and TLS citations into upstream_refs; this remains one permission clause.

requirements.title: Prohibit 0-RTT for non-replayable transactions
requirements.statement: The 0-RTT mechanism MUST NOT be used to send DNS requests that are not replayable transactions.
notes: Single prohibition clause; no split needed.

requirements.title: Classify QUERY and NOTIFY transactions as replayable
requirements.statement: Transactions with an OPCODE of QUERY or NOTIFY MUST be considered replayable.
notes: Trimmed for canonical requirement wording while preserving the referenced normative source.

requirements.title: Allow clients to use session resumption and 0-RTT when supported
requirements.statement: A client MAY take advantage of the session resumption and 0-RTT mechanisms supported by QUIC transport [RFC9000] and QUIC TLS [RFC9001] if the server supports them.

requirements.title: Consider session-resumption privacy before enabling 0-RTT
requirements.statement: Clients SHOULD consider potential privacy issues associated with session resumption before deciding to use this mechanism and specifically evaluate the trade-offs presented in the various sections of this document.

requirements.title: Allow session resumption with or without 0-RTT
requirements.statement: Servers MAY support session resumption with or without 0-RTT using the mechanisms described in Section 4.6.1 of [RFC9001].

requirements.title: Do not immediately process non-replayable 0-RTT transactions
requirements.statement: Servers supporting 0-RTT MUST NOT immediately process non-replayable transactions received in 0-RTT data.

requirements.title: Handle non-replayable 0-RTT transactions by queue, refusal, or close
requirements.statement: Servers supporting 0-RTT MUST adopt one of the following behaviors: queue the offending transaction and only process it after the QUIC handshake has been completed, reply to the offending transaction with a response code REFUSED and an EDE "Too Early", or close the connection with the error code DOQ_PROTOCOL_ERROR.

requirements.title: Ignore EDNS(0) UDP payload size
requirements.statement: DoQ implementations MUST ignore the EDNS(0) UDP payload size when determining DoQ message size.

requirements.title: Enforce the 65535-byte DoQ message maximum
requirements.statement: DoQ implementations MUST enforce a maximum DNS message size of 65535 bytes.

requirements.title: Support connection reuse
requirements.statement: Both clients and servers SHOULD support connection reuse by sending multiple queries and responses over a single persistent QUIC connection.

requirements.title: Send queries concurrently
requirements.statement: DNS clients SHOULD send their queries concurrently over the QUIC streams on a QUIC connection.

requirements.title: Do not wait for an outstanding reply before sending the next query
requirements.statement: When a DNS client sends multiple queries to a server over a QUIC connection, it SHOULD NOT wait for an outstanding reply before sending the next query.

requirements.title: Use QUIC idle timeout mechanisms for long-duration connections
requirements.statement: Clients that want to maintain long duration DoQ connections SHOULD use the idle timeout mechanisms defined in Section 10.1 of [RFC9000], the QUIC transport specification.

requirements.title: Do not send EDNS TCP keepalive on DoQ connections
requirements.statement: Clients and servers MUST not send the edns-tcp-keepalive EDNS(0) Option [RFC7828] in any messages sent on a DoQ connection.
notes: Normalized modal phrasing to keep exactly one uppercase normative keyword in the statement.

requirements.title: Use resumption tickets only once
requirements.statement: Clients SHOULD use resumption tickets only once, as specified in Appendix C.4 of RFC8446.

requirements.title: Avoid resumption after connectivity changes
requirements.statement: By default, clients SHOULD NOT use session resumption if the client's connectivity has changed.

requirements.title: Use address validation tokens only with resumption
requirements.statement: Clients SHOULD only use the address validation tokens when they are also using session resumption.

requirements.title: Issue long-lived resumption tickets
requirements.statement: Servers SHOULD issue session resumption tickets with a sufficiently long lifetime.
notes: RFC 9250 gives 6 hours as an example lifetime.

requirements.title: Implement anti-replay mechanisms
requirements.statement: Servers SHOULD implement the anti-replay mechanisms specified in Section 8 of RFC8446.

requirements.title: Default to privacy-preserving new sessions
requirements.statement: Clients SHOULD prioritize privacy and start new sessions when connectivity changes.
notes: Trimmed wording while preserving the same testable obligation.

requirements.title: Send responses promptly on the specific stream
requirements.statement: A DoQ implementation SHOULD send responses on the specific stream as soon as possible, without waiting for availability of responses for previously opened streams.

requirements.title: Handle concurrent IXFR requests
requirements.statement: DoQ servers MUST be able to handle multiple concurrent IXFR requests on a single QUIC connection.

requirements.title: Handle concurrent AXFR requests
requirements.statement: DoQ servers MUST be able to handle multiple concurrent AXFR requests on a single QUIC connection.

requirements.title: Use one QUIC connection for AXFR and IXFR to the same primary
requirements.statement: The same QUIC connection MUST be used for both AXFR and IXFR requests to the same primary.

requirements.title: Send queued zone transfer requests in parallel
requirements.statement: Queued zone transfer requests MUST be sent in parallel as soon as they are queued, without waiting for a response before sending the next query on the connection.

requirements.title: Intermingled response streams
requirements.statement: The response streams for each request MAY be sent intermingled as soon as they are available.

requirements.title: Use RFC 9000 flow control mechanisms
requirements.statement: Servers and clients MUST use the flow control mechanisms defined in Section 4 of RFC 9000.

requirements.title: Specify aggregate data limit
requirements.statement: Flow control mechanisms MUST allow clients and servers to specify how much data can be sent on the union of all streams.

requirements.title: Specify per-stream data limit
requirements.statement: Flow control mechanisms MUST allow clients and servers to specify how much data can be sent on a stream.

requirements.title: Specify stream creation limit
requirements.statement: Flow control mechanisms MUST allow clients and servers to specify how many streams can be created.

requirements.title: Server flow control limits
requirements.statement: Servers MUST use global and per-stream flow control limits to control how much data clients can send.

requirements.title: Client flow control limits
requirements.statement: Clients MUST use global and per-stream flow control limits to control how much data servers can send.

requirements.title: Handshake transport parameters carry flow control limits
requirements.statement: Flow control limits MUST be specified in transport parameters exchanged during the connection handshake.

requirements.title: Use initial connection flow control limits for 0-RTT
requirements.statement: The flow control limits received in the initial connection MUST control how many requests and how much data clients can send using 0-RTT data in a resumed connection.

requirements.title: State-preserving 0-RTT transactions
requirements.statement: Transactions allowed by Section 4.5 MUST preserve the long-term state of the server.

requirements.title: Mitigate traffic analysis attacks
requirements.statement: Implementations SHOULD use the mechanisms defined in Section 5.4 to mitigate this attack.

requirements.title: Use the DoQ ALPN identification sequence
requirements.statement: The DoQ ALPN identification sequence MUST be 0x64 0x6F 0x71 ("doq").

requirements.title: Use a 62-bit registry space
requirements.statement: The DNS-over-QUIC Error Codes registry MUST govern a 62-bit space.
notes: Normalized from a descriptive registry invariant.

requirements.title: Assign permanent registrations in the 0x00 to 0x3f range with approved policies
requirements.statement: Permanent registrations for values between 0x00 and 0x3f inclusive MUST be assigned using Standards Action or IESG Approval as defined in Sections 4.9 and 4.10 of RFC8126.
notes: Normalized from a figure bullet.

requirements.title: Assign specification-required permanent registrations above 0x3f
requirements.statement: Permanent registrations for values larger than 0x3f MUST be assigned using the Specification Required policy as defined in RFC8126.
notes: Corrected the requirement wording to match the source unit.

requirements.title: Require Expert Review for provisional registrations above 0x3f
requirements.statement: Provisional registrations for values larger than 0x3f MUST require Expert Review, as defined in Section 4.5 of RFC8126.
notes: This source unit is a standalone normative bullet and should not be skipped.

requirements.title: Specification optional for provisional registrations
requirements.statement: The Specification field MAY be omitted for provisional registrations.
notes: Normalized from a field-definition optionality statement.

requirements.title: Allow summary descriptions when a specification reference exists
requirements.statement: The Description field MAY be a summary if a Specification reference is provided.

requirements.title: Allow date updates on provisional registrations without expert review
requirements.statement: A request to update the Date on any provisional registration MAY be made without review from the designated expert(s).
notes: Normalized from expert-review waiver language.

requirements.title: Assign 0x0 to DOQ_NO_ERROR
requirements.statement: The value 0x0 MUST be assigned to DOQ_NO_ERROR.

requirements.title: Assign 0x1 to DOQ_INTERNAL_ERROR
requirements.statement: The value 0x1 MUST be assigned to DOQ_INTERNAL_ERROR.

requirements.title: Assign 0x2 to DOQ_PROTOCOL_ERROR
requirements.statement: The value 0x2 MUST be assigned to DOQ_PROTOCOL_ERROR.

requirements.title: Assign 0x3 to DOQ_REQUEST_CANCELLED
requirements.statement: The value 0x3 MUST be assigned to DOQ_REQUEST_CANCELLED.

requirements.title: Assign 0x4 to DOQ_EXCESSIVE_LOAD
requirements.statement: The value 0x4 MUST be assigned to DOQ_EXCESSIVE_LOAD.

requirements.title: Assign 0x5 to DOQ_UNSPECIFIED_ERROR
requirements.statement: The value 0x5 MUST be assigned to DOQ_UNSPECIFIED_ERROR.

requirements.title: Assign 0xd098ea5e to DOQ_ERROR_RESERVED
requirements.statement: The value 0xd098ea5e MUST be assigned to DOQ_ERROR_RESERVED.

requirements.title: Allow NOTIFY in 0-RTT data
requirements.statement: A NOTIFY MAY be sent in 0-RTT data.

requirements.title: Use a Strict usage profile for DoQ stubs
requirements.statement: DoQ stubs SHOULD use a Strict usage profile.

requirements.title: Opportunistic usage profile fallback
requirements.statement: An implementation using the Opportunistic usage profile SHOULD fall back to DoT or cleartext DNS if the DoQ connection attempt fails.

requirements.title: Back off after DoQ failure
requirements.statement: Implementations using the Opportunistic profile SHOULD back off from DoQ for at least the timeout value after the failure.

requirements.title: Key-pinned endpoints retry DoQ aggressively
requirements.statement: Key-pinned endpoints SHOULD retry DoQ more aggressively after a failure.

requirements.title: DoQ failure cache
requirements.statement: An implementation using the Opportunistic profile SHOULD record DoQ failures in a cache and avoid repeated attempts.

requirements.title: Configurable backoff timeout
requirements.statement: The backoff timeout MUST be configurable.

requirements.title: Be conservative when falling back to cleartext
requirements.statement: Implementations SHOULD be conservative when falling back to cleartext DNS.

requirements.title: Enforce amplification limit
requirements.statement: Servers supporting 0-RTT MUST enforce the 3x anti-amplification limit specified in RFC 9000.

requirements.title: Use QUIC Retry and address validation
requirements.statement: Servers SHOULD use QUIC Retry and address validation to protect against amplification attacks.

requirements.title: Add EDNS(0) padding to DoQ messages
requirements.statement: Implementations SHOULD add EDNS(0) padding to DoQ messages to mitigate traffic analysis.

requirements.title: Padding policy aligned with RFC 7830/8467
requirements.statement: The padding policy SHOULD follow the recommendations in RFC 7830 and RFC 8467.

requirements.title: Padding boundary and fuzz tests
requirements.statement: Padding implementations MUST include boundary and fuzz tests.

requirements.title: Padding overhead benchmark
requirements.statement: Padding implementations SHOULD include benchmark coverage for padding overhead.
